title: Off Work on Time for Once
teaser: After the last surgery of the afternoon wraps up smoothly, Hiroko stands outside the nurses' station studying a shopping street food map in dead earnest.

choices.choice_hlv2_083_1: "You caught me. Getting to tag along with a food expert for an upgrade once in a while really isn't bad at all."
choices.choice_hlv2_083_2: "You seem a lot more talkative tonight than you usually are at the hospital."
choices.finish_hiroko_lv2: Watch Hiroko head into the station

nodes.hlv2_001: At 4:10 PM, the main shadowless lamp in Operating Room 2 had already been switched off, leaving only the soft overhead lighting.
nodes.hlv2_002: The last scheduled surgery of the day had just concluded smoothly, and the patient had been escorted to the recovery room. Standing beside the instrument table, Hiroko Sugimura briskly finished counting the final set of hemostats and suture needles, then pushed the verified sign-off sheet toward the charting desk.
nodes.hlv2_003: Ryuji Sakaguchi peeled off his sterile gloves, tossed them into the medical waste bin, and walked up to the charting desk to pick up a pen. Before he could even speak, Hiroko had already flipped another folder open to the exact page and placed it steadily beside his hand.
nodes.hlv2_004: "Here is the postoperative order confirmation sheet, and this is the special instrument preparation checklist for tomorrow morning's two surgeries—I've already highlighted the key items according to your usual preferences."
nodes.hlv2_005: Sakaguchi's fingers paused as he took the folder, and he couldn't help looking up at her.
nodes.hlv2_006: "How do you always know what I'm about to ask before I even say a word?"
nodes.hlv2_007: Hiroko's eyes curved into a gentle, slightly proud smile.
nodes.hlv2_008: "Hehe. Work alongside you for this long, Doctor, and I'm bound to pick up a little experience."
nodes.hlv2_009: As Sakaguchi signed the postoperative record, he asked casually:
nodes.hlv2_010: "Am I really that easy to read?"
nodes.hlv2_011: Hiroko tilted her head slightly, tapping her chin lightly with a fingertip:
nodes.hlv2_013: Sakaguchi stopped his pen and looked at her:
nodes.hlv2_015: Hiroko let out a soft giggle, her eyes curving into lovely crescents:
nodes.hlv2_017: Just then, the outer intercom of the operating room chimed once, and a ward nurse poked her head in through the doorway to report:
nodes.hlv2_018: "Excuse me, Dr. Sakaguchi, Nurse Sugimura. The inpatient ward just called to ask—since this afternoon's operations finished early, the family of the inguinal hernia repair patient in Bed 42, originally scheduled for the second slot tomorrow morning, is wondering if we could move the surgery up to this evening instead?"
nodes.hlv2_019: Sakaguchi glanced at the wall clock. It was just past four-ten, and for patients who had already completed admission procedures, hospital policy did allow surgeries to be scheduled into the evening or even late at night depending on actual circumstances.
nodes.hlv2_020: Sakaguchi pulled up Bed 42's electronic chart and looked it over:
nodes.hlv2_021: "Bed 42 is already admitted, and all of the preoperative lab work came back this afternoon. As long as we confirm fasting status and anesthesia readiness with the ward, adding an uncomplicated indirect inguinal hernia repair to tonight's schedule is medically feasible..."
nodes.hlv2_022: He turned his head, habitually consulting his partner beside him:
nodes.hlv2_023: "Hiroko, what do you think from the OR scheduling side?"
nodes.hlv2_024: The relaxed smile on Hiroko's face faded slightly as her gaze swept earnestly across the scheduling board and instrument turnover log before she spoke in a clear, structured tone:
nodes.hlv2_025: "From the standpoint of medical readiness and operating time, it is certainly something we could consider. However, Dr. Sakaguchi, we already performed three consecutive surgeries this afternoon, and all of the standard surgical instrument sets from that batch were just sent down for central washing and sterilization; on top of that, one of the night-shift nurses is on scheduled rotation tonight, leaving the on-duty night nursing staff very short-handed."
nodes.hlv2_026: She reached out a finger and tapped lightly on the instrument turnover and handover column at the bottom of the schedule board:
nodes.hlv2_027: "This patient has no signs of incarceration or emergency indications. If we add the case now and it runs past the five o'clock shift handover, not only would we have to open tonight's sole emergency backup instrument set and backup operating room, the night nursing team would also be stretched thin between instrument turnover and postoperative monitoring—if a true emergency surgery comes in overnight, the OR's backup resources would be put in a very tight spot."
nodes.hlv2_028: Hiroko met his gaze, her voice remaining gentle yet firm:
nodes.hlv2_029: "Since Bed 42 is a standard elective procedure, I believe keeping the original schedule and performing it tomorrow morning—once the day-shift staff and standard instrument sets are all in place—is the safer choice for both the patient and the operating room team."
nodes.hlv2_030: After a brief moment of thought, Sakaguchi closed the schedule clipboard without hesitation and nodded:
nodes.hlv2_031: "You're right. Even if adding the case tonight is medically feasible, we can't tie up the night shift's staffing and emergency backup resources just to move an elective surgery forward."
nodes.hlv2_032: Turning toward the ward nurse at the door, he gave a decisive instruction:
nodes.hlv2_033: "Please let the patient in Bed 42 and their family know that in order to ensure the best possible operating room preparation and postoperative care, the surgery will remain on its original schedule and proceed on time tomorrow morning. I'll stop by the ward shortly to explain to them in person."
nodes.hlv2_035: Once the ward nurse had left, Hiroko let out a quiet breath of relief and looked up at Sakaguchi:
nodes.hlv2_036: "I'm sorry, Doctor. Speaking up against your suggestion right in front of the ward nurse just now might have come across a bit too blunt... Still, hearing that you were willing to reconsider the schedule really was a relief."
nodes.hlv2_038: "What are you apologizing for? You kept a check on night-shift turnover and our emergency reserves for me—I should be thanking you. If the OR nurses simply went along with whatever the lead surgeon said, that would be the real problem."
nodes.hlv2_039: A bright spark of joy flickered in Hiroko's eyes as the corners of her lips lifted softly:
nodes.hlv2_040: "Thank you for listening to my input, Doctor. I'll go finish confirming the final handover log, then—to think we'll actually get to clock out on time at five today."
nodes.hlv2_041: After stopping by the ward to briefly explain the situation to the family in Bed 42, Ryuji Sakaguchi returned to the locker room and changed into his casual clothes.
nodes.hlv2_042: The clock hands had just reached ten past five. Free for once from staying late to write charts or cover a night shift, Sakaguchi walked lightly out of the staff corridor, ready to leave the hospital.
nodes.hlv2_043: As he passed the hallway outside the surgical nurses' station, his footsteps suddenly came to a halt.
nodes.hlv2_044: There stood Hiroko Sugimura, already changed into a soft beige-apricot knit cardigan over a light plaid skirt—yet instead of heading toward the main entrance, she was standing alone beside the side counter of the nurses' station. With her head lowered and both hands holding an open tri-fold brochure, her delicate brows were slightly knitted, her gaze as intensely focused as if she were studying a baffling clinical case.
nodes.hlv2_046: "Hiroko? Still haven't headed out yet—was there something in the handover log that didn't match up?"
nodes.hlv2_047: Startled, Hiroko jerked her head up:
nodes.hlv2_049: Seeing Sakaguchi looking with concern at the leaflet in her hands, a faint blush crept across Hiroko's fair cheeks, and she sheepishly turned the full-color brochure around.
nodes.hlv2_050: Printed across the brochure wasn't a medical chart at all—it was packed from edge to edge with photos of dorayaki, omurice, and seasonal limited-edition parfaits.
nodes.hlv2_051: "I-it's not work! I finished the entire handover ten minutes ago... I was just seriously trying to figure out which shop in the shopping district to go eat at tonight."
nodes.hlv2_052: Staring at the colorful shopping street food map, Sakaguchi was momentarily at a loss for words:
nodes.hlv2_053: "...With how serious your expression was just now, I thought something had gone wrong with the instrument sets for one of tomorrow's surgeries."
nodes.hlv2_054: Hiroko burst into a soft laugh, hugging the brochure to her chest as she gave a playful wink and teased:
nodes.hlv2_055: "Hehe, in your eyes, Dr. Sakaguchi, do you think my head is still filled with nothing but hemostats and sterile gauze even after I take off my nurse's uniform? It's rare enough that we get to clock out on time at five—what to have for dinner is a matter of top priority."
nodes.hlv2_057: "Fair enough. Did your research turn up a conclusion, then?"
nodes.hlv2_058: Hiroko pointed to a shop in the corner of the brochure illustrated with a warm yellow lantern, a hint of eager anticipation brightening her eyes:
nodes.hlv2_059: "There's actually a little place in the shopping district that serves Japanese-style Western dishes and freshly baked sweets. I've heard colleagues mention it several times and have been wanting to try it, but I usually get off work too late to make it in time."
nodes.hlv2_060: Speaking up to here, she raised her eyes toward Sakaguchi and extended a natural invitation:
nodes.hlv2_061: "Since you also happened to finish on time today, Dr. Sakaguchi, if you don't have other plans for the evening... would you like to go try it together?"
nodes.hlv2_065: "Mhm. Back in the operating room just now, didn't you say you wanted to thank me for helping keep check on the schedule? Besides, their dinner set for two lets you pick two extra side dishes—it'd be such a waste to go eat there all by myself."
nodes.hlv2_067: "When Nurse Sugimura puts it like that, how could I refuse? Let's go—I'm getting hungry myself."
nodes.hlv2_068: Hiroko's eyes lit up as she happily picked up her handbag:
nodes.hlv2_069: "Wonderful! Let's head over right away—if we go now, we definitely won't have to wait in line!"
nodes.hlv2_070: Rows of warm streetlamps had come on along the evening shopping arcade, and the steady stream of commuters, housewives shopping for dinner, and students heading home from school made the street feel lively and welcoming.
nodes.hlv2_071: The little bistro Hiroko led him to was tucked around a corner midway down the arcade, its wooden tables and chairs wiped spotless and gleaming, the air rich with the buttery aroma of beef stew and sweet baked red beans.
nodes.hlv2_072: Brought to their table were a steaming hamburger steak set meal and golden, fluffy thick-rolled tamagoyaki, alongside a chestnut matcha parfait Hiroko had specially ordered on the side.
nodes.hlv2_073: Pressing her hands together with a cheerful "Thank you for the meal," Hiroko picked up a small piece of the thick-rolled egg with her chopsticks, popped it into her mouth, and narrowed her eyes in pure satisfaction:
nodes.hlv2_074: "Mmm... the balance between the dashi stock and the sweetness is just right! No wonder everyone recommends this place—coming here today was definitely the right call."
nodes.hlv2_075: Using the serving chopsticks, she placed a piece of tamagoyaki onto Sakaguchi's small plate and urged him with a smile:
nodes.hlv2_076: "Try some too, Dr. Sakaguchi! It's so much more tender than the kind the hospital cafeteria serves on Wednesdays."
nodes.hlv2_078: "It really is good. I had no idea you knew the little shops in the shopping arcade this well."
nodes.hlv2_079: Resting her cheek lightly on her hand, Hiroko smiled:
nodes.hlv2_080: "Work keeps me busy on most days, sure, but whenever I walk past the arcade I secretly jot down promising-looking shops in my phone's notes. You, on the other hand, Dr. Sakaguchi—when we looked at the menu just now, you decided on the hamburger steak set in under ten seconds. You order dinner just as briskly as you call for instruments at the operating table."
nodes.hlv2_081: "I'm used to eating alone, so I just pick whatever catches my eye first without thinking too much about it."
nodes.hlv2_082: Hiroko shot him a teasing glance:
nodes.hlv2_083: "I knew it. When you're home by yourself, Doctor, don't tell me you just make do with instant curry or convenience store bento every night?"
nodes.hlv2_085: "You caught me. Getting to tag along with a food expert for an upgrade once in a while really isn't bad at all."
nodes.hlv2_086: Scooping up a spoonful of her matcha parfait, Hiroko curved her eyes smugly:
nodes.hlv2_087: "Hehe, then the next time we both manage to get off work on time, I'll generously take you through every single shop on my list one by one, Dr. Sakaguchi."
nodes.hlv2_088: Sakaguchi looked at her bright, smiling face:
nodes.hlv2_089: "You seem a lot more talkative tonight than you usually are at the hospital."
nodes.hlv2_090: Hiroko's hand paused over her ice cream before she gave a playful wink:
nodes.hlv2_091: "Because at the hospital, I'm Nurse Sugimura who has to help keep everything in check for everyone. Now that we've clocked out for the day, I don't need to keep up my nurse's poise at the dinner table."
nodes.hlv2_092: Over the steaming dinner, the two chatted about their favorite flavors, movies they had seen recently, and how they liked to spend their days off. She would wrinkle her nose ever so slightly when biting into a tangy pickle, and laugh right out loud whenever something funny came up.
nodes.hlv2_093: When they went to pay the bill, the shopkeeper handed over three slips of paper printed with red lettering, beaming from ear to ear:
nodes.hlv2_094: "Thank you very much! The shopping arcade is holding a pre-weekend Fukubiki lottery right now—your bill qualifies for three draws! The lottery booth is just fifty meters to the right outside the door, so go try your luck!"
nodes.hlv2_095: As Hiroko took the three lottery tickets, her eyes lit up at once.
nodes.hlv2_096: In the small plaza at the center of the shopping arcade stood a lottery booth festooned with red-and-white bunting flags, an octagonal wooden rotary lottery drum resting on the counter.
nodes.hlv2_097: Perched on the very top shelf of the prize rack was a plump white cat mascot cushion—the emblem of the shopping arcade—waving its paw endearingly at passersby.
nodes.hlv2_098: Stopping in front of the booth, Hiroko's gaze was immediately captured by the white cat cushion.
nodes.hlv2_099: "Wow... Dr. Sakaguchi, look at that kitty cushion up on top—it's so fluffy and adorable!"
nodes.hlv2_100: Sakaguchi handed all three tickets over to her:
nodes.hlv2_101: "All three tickets are right here. Go give it a spin—maybe you'll hit the grand prize on the first try."
nodes.hlv2_102: Happily taking the tickets and handing them to the booth attendant, Hiroko took a deep breath, rolled up the sleeve of her knit cardigan, and gripped the handle:
nodes.hlv2_103: "Then I won't hold back! Watch this—"
nodes.hlv2_104: The wooden drum rumbled around a full turn, and with a crisp clack, a pure white wooden ball dropped out.
nodes.hlv2_105: The booth attendant rang a small brass bell:
nodes.hlv2_106: "Congratulations! Consolation prize—one pack of pocket tissues!"
nodes.hlv2_107: Hiroko blinked in surprise as she took the tissues:
nodes.hlv2_109: Flexing her fingers with a touch of stubbornness, she took hold of the handle again:
nodes.hlv2_110: "I spun it too fast just now—I'll turn it more slowly this time!"
nodes.hlv2_112: Another unmistakable white ball rolled into the tray.
nodes.hlv2_113: Beaming, the attendant handed over a second pack of tissues:
nodes.hlv2_115: Staring at the two neat packs of pocket tissues in her hand, Hiroko fell silent for two seconds as her gaze gradually turned dead serious.
nodes.hlv2_116: Fixing her eyes on the octagonal wooden drum, her delicate brows arched slightly as she analyzed it in earnest:
nodes.hlv2_117: "That's strange... On the second turn just now, I distinctly heard the clink of a colored ball with a slightly different center of gravity inside. As long as I control the reverse angle properly, I can definitely shake a colored ball out on the next spin!"
nodes.hlv2_118: Watching from beside her, Sakaguchi could barely hold back a laugh:
nodes.hlv2_119: "Hiroko, all the balls inside a lottery drum like that weigh the exact same—there's no angle trick to it. If this last ticket doesn't hit either, we should probably wrap it up."
nodes.hlv2_120: Hiroko turned her head, puffing her cheeks out slightly:
nodes.hlv2_121: "No way! Third time's the charm, and I've already got a feel for the handle! Besides, buying two boxes of throat lozenges at the general store next door comes with one bonus ticket—if this spin misses, I'm going over to trade for one more try!"
nodes.hlv2_122: Sakaguchi didn't know whether to laugh or cry:
nodes.hlv2_123: "How does someone who's normally so scientific in the operating room get this competitive with a wooden box at a lottery booth?"
nodes.hlv2_125: "Work is work, and lotteries are all about momentum! Just watch closely, Doctor!"
nodes.hlv2_126: Holding her breath, she gripped the handle with total concentration, turned it half a circle at an unhurried pace, and gave a gentle flick backward—
nodes.hlv2_128: A bright yellow wooden ball rolled down the chute.
nodes.hlv2_129: The booth attendant rang the brass handbell vigorously:
nodes.hlv2_130: "Ding-ding-ding! Congratulations to the young lady—Fourth Prize: one shopping arcade white cat mascot mini keychain!"
nodes.hlv2_131: Even though it wasn't the large cushion on the top shelf, Hiroko's eyes lit up and she let out a delighted cheer as soon as she received the tiny metal keychain shaped like the beckoning white cat:
nodes.hlv2_132: "Awesome! See, Dr. Sakaguchi? I told you a colored ball would come out once I got the feel for it!"
nodes.hlv2_133: She held the little keychain up in front of Sakaguchi and gave it a proud shake, her eyes curving like crescent moons.
nodes.hlv2_134: Looking from the thumb-sized keychain in her hand to the identical merchandise clearly price-tagged in the general store window next door, Sakaguchi couldn't help speaking honestly:
nodes.hlv2_135: "Winning it is impressive, sure... though Hiroko, the exact same keychain in that shop window looks like it costs three hundred yen. Buying one outright might've been cheaper than buying extra items for lottery tickets."
nodes.hlv2_136: The triumphant smile on Hiroko's face froze on the spot.
nodes.hlv2_137: Lowering the keychain, she puffed her cheeks and glared at Sakaguchi, unable to keep from complaining:
nodes.hlv2_138: "Meanie! You really have no sense of romance, Doctor!"
nodes.hlv2_139: Sakaguchi blinked, then chuckled and raised his hands in surrender:
nodes.hlv2_140: "My mistake—I spoke out of turn. A trophy won with your own hands definitely means a lot more than buying one off the shelf."
nodes.hlv2_141: Giving a soft humph, Hiroko carefully clipped the white cat keychain onto the zipper of her commuter bag, then pressed one of the two tissue packs she had drawn into Sakaguchi's hand:
nodes.hlv2_142: "This pack is for you, as a souvenir for keeping me company at the lottery booth. And no complaining that it's cheap!"
nodes.hlv2_143: Smiling, Sakaguchi tucked the tissues into his jacket pocket:
nodes.hlv2_144: "Don't worry, I'll keep it with me."
nodes.hlv2_145: Leaving the lively shopping arcade behind, the two chatted as they strolled along the quiet walkway until, before they knew it, they had reached the street corner in front of the train station.
nodes.hlv2_146: The night breeze rustled through the leaves of the street trees, carrying a pleasant, refreshing coolness.
nodes.hlv2_147: At the steps leading up to the station platform, Hiroko stopped and turned to face Sakaguchi, the soft halo of the streetlamp falling across her smiling eyes.
nodes.hlv2_148: "Thank you for walking me all the way here tonight, Doctor. It's been such a long time since I got to eat out and browse the shops so carefree after work—I really had a wonderful time today."
nodes.hlv2_149: "Same here. Thanks to you leading the way, not only did I get to eat at an authentic local spot, I also got to witness Nurse Sugimura's prowess at the lottery wheel firsthand."
nodes.hlv2_150: With a faint blush on her cheeks, Hiroko lightly fingered the white cat keychain on her bag and looked up at him with a smile:
nodes.hlv2_151: "Come to think of it, I discovered something new today too—when we only worked together in the operating room and the wards, I always thought of you as someone who was calm and serious no matter the occasion, Dr. Sakaguchi. I didn't expect that hanging out after work, you're actually quite an interesting person."
nodes.hlv2_153: "'Quite an interesting person'? What's that supposed to mean?"
nodes.hlv2_154: Watching him press for an answer, the corners of Hiroko's lips curved into a playful arc as she teased him on purpose:
nodes.hlv2_157: Hiroko tilted her head with a beaming smile:
nodes.hlv2_159: The two stood looking at each other beneath the streetlamp for a quiet moment as the evening breeze drifted across the intersection.
nodes.hlv2_160: Taking a gentle breath, Hiroko spoke up on her own:
nodes.hlv2_161: "There are still quite a few shops on that food map we looked at earlier that I haven't tried yet. If we ever manage to clock out on time like today again... let's go out for another walk together, Dr. Sakaguchi."
nodes.hlv2_162: Sakaguchi nodded with a warm smile:
nodes.hlv2_164: Stepping up two stairs toward the platform, Hiroko suddenly seemed to remember something; turning back around, she gave a playful wink and teased him with a hint of mischief:
nodes.hlv2_165: "Though next time, there might not be such a good opportunity, you know?"
nodes.hlv2_167: Seeing the slightly stunned look on Sakaguchi's face, Hiroko finally couldn't help covering her lips with a soft laugh and giving him a gentle wave:
nodes.hlv2_169: Leaving behind that light-hearted farewell, she turned around, the hem of her skirt swaying gently with her buoyant steps as she blended into the bright lights of the station.
